stem: When teaching transplant recipients about candidemia, which clinical significance aligns with standard references?

options.text: A significant infection associated with high mortality and graft loss
A benign colonization that never affects graft function
An infection limited exclusively to the pretransplant period
A condition that never causes mortality in transplant recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidemia is described as a significant infection associated with high mortality and graft loss, warranting prompt evaluation and treatment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Candidemia is a significant invasive infection rather than benign colonization without graft impact.
rationale_incorrect.C: Candidemia is a post-transplant complication rather than being limited to pretransplant.
rationale_incorrect.D: High mortality is specifically cited rather than candidemia being harmless.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → fungal infections → Candidemia → i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Significant infection associated with high mortality and graft loss

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → fungal infections → Candidemia → i. (high mortality and graft loss); PDF p. 736 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Candidemia severity epidemiology angle distinct from Candida prophylaxis timing (cctc-3153) and fluconazole interaction (cctc-3154); anchor verified on Cupples p. 736.

stem: A recently transplanted recipient develops fever, lymphadenopathy, and a new rash. Which fungal-infection teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Candidemia may present with fever, lymphadenopathy, and rash
Fever with rash always indicates acute cellular rejection and never infection
Lymphadenopathy excludes candidemia from the differential
Candidemia never causes fever in immunosuppressed recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidemia symptoms may include fever, lymphadenopathy, and rash, and diagnosis includes blood cultures with evaluation for abscess or cardiac vegetations when central venous lines are present.

rationale_incorrect.B: Fever with rash may reflect candidemia or other infections and requires evaluation rather than assuming rejection alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lymphadenopathy is among cited candidemia symptoms rather than excluding it.
rationale_incorrect.D: Fever is specifically listed among candidemia symptoms.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → fungal infections → Candidemia → ii.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → fungal infections → Candidemia → ii. (fever, lymphadenopathy, rash); PDF p. 736 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Candidemia presentation angle distinct from candidemia severity recall (cctc-3157) and pediatric Candida rash (cctc-3155); anchor verified on Cupples p. 736.

stem: A lung transplant recipient with prolonged surgery and reexploration develops isolated fever months after transplant. Which Aspergillus risk or presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Extended operative time greater than 12 hours and reexploration are cited risk factors
Aspergillus occurs only when operative time is under 30 minutes
Reexploration eliminates Aspergillus risk after lung transplantation
Operative duration never influences post-transplant fungal risk

explanation.rationale_correct: Aspergillus risk factors include extended operative time greater than 12 hours, reexplorations, retransplantation, neutropenia, high immunosuppressive load, and prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics.

rationale_incorrect.B: Extended operative time greater than 12 hours is a cited risk factor rather than very short surgery alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Reexploration increases risk rather than eliminating Aspergillus concern.
rationale_incorrect.D: Operative time and reexploration are specifically listed among risk factors.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → fungal infections → Aspergillus → iv.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → fungal infections → Aspergillus → iv. (extended operative time >12 hours and reexploration as risk factors); PDF p. 737 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Aspergillus operative-risk angle distinct from later-timing epidemiology in combo (cctc-3156) and pulmonary primary-site recall; anchor verified on Cupples p. 737.

stem: A coordinator is updating candidemia and Aspergillus teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Candidemia is associated with high mortality and graft loss.
Candidemia may present with fever, lymphadenopathy, and rash.
Aspergillus infection may occur 6 months or more post-transplant.
Lungs are never a site of Aspergillus infection.

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidemia severity, candidemia symptoms, and later Aspergillus timing are supported. Statement IV is false because lungs are the most common primary site of Aspergillus infection.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—Aspergillus may occur 6 months or more post-transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because pulmonary involvement is specifically described.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → fungal infections → Candidemia and Aspergillus
primary_anchor.quote_hint: high mortality and graft loss … Fever … Lymphadenopathy … Rash … Later infection, occurring 6 months or more posttransplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → fungal infections → Candidemia → i.–ii. (mortality/graft loss; fever, lymphadenopathy, rash); PDF p. 736 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → fungal infections → Aspergillus → i.–ii. (later infection ≥6 months; lungs most common primary site); PDF p. 737 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Candidemia/Aspergillus combo distinct from Candida/Aspergillus combo (cctc-3156) and early fungal-risk combo (cctc-3152); corroborating locators on p. 736 and p. 737 verified.
